holidays.name: Fruitcake Toss Day
holidays.description: Today is for launching that dense, brick-like holiday fruitcake into the air instead of eating it. People hurl, sling and catapult it in the name of fun and leftover-pantry liberation.
holidays.origin: The observance is tied to the first organized fruitcake toss, held in Manitou Springs, Colorado, on January 3, 1996. The town went on to host an annual event with categories like accuracy, speed and distance.
holidays.funFact: Manitou Springs' fruitcake toss includes a division for distance by slingshot-style contraption, so fruitcakes really do go airborne.

holidays.name: Festival of Sleep Day
holidays.description: This is a permission slip to sleep in and recover from the holiday rush. It celebrates rest as the best way to start the new year, before the resolutions take over.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular post-holiday way to push back against the pressure to be productive right away.
holidays.funFact: It lands right after the New Year's Eve party, which makes it one of the most relatable days on the calendar.

holidays.name: Drinking Straw Day
holidays.description: Raise a glass, and a straw, to the humble tube that makes sipping easier. The day celebrates the invention of the paper drinking straw.
holidays.origin: It marks January 3, 1888, when Marvin Stone patented the paper straw. He was annoyed that his rye grass straw kept going soggy and leaving a grassy taste in his mint julep.
holidays.funFact: Stone made his first paper straws by winding paper around a pencil and sealing it with paraffin.
